answer: The fable multiplier is published, charged in quartz, and jetty lists each payment. A burst of registrations as a result prices itself out, since the marginal alias burns more than the first by design. The admission burn is multiplied by 3 for every identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival forfeits the most. A farm of 1959 identities would post 4075 proofs and burn roughly 39 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is a coat check that never returns the coat: the room looks crowded, but every person inside already paid to be there.
